title.zh: 卷二百七十五 列傳第三十四 劉福 安守忠 孔守正 譚延美 元達 常思德 尹繼倫 薛超 丁罕 趙瑫 郭密 傅思讓 李斌 田仁朗 劉謙
title.en: Volume 275 Biographies 34: Liu Fu, An Shouzhong, Kong Shouzheng, Tan Yanmei, Yuan Da, Chang Side, Yin Jilun, Xue Chao, Ding Han, Zhao Tao, Guo Mi, Fu Sirang, Li Bin, Tian Renlang, Liu Qian
title.raw: 卷二百七十五 列傳第三十四 劉福 安守忠 孔守正 譚延美 元達 常思德 尹繼倫 薛超 丁罕 趙瑫 郭密 傅思讓 李斌 田仁朗 劉謙 Volume 275 Biographies 34: Liu Fu, An Shouzhong, Kong Shouzheng, Tan Yanmei, Yuan Da, Chang Side, Yin Jilun, Xue Chao, Ding Han, Zhao Tao, Guo Mi, Fu Sirang, Li Bin, Tian Renlang, Liu Qian

sentences.zh: 劉福，徐州下邳人。

translations.literal: Liu Fu was a native of Xiapi in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu was from Xiapi in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，魁岸有膂力。

translations.literal: In youth he was unrestrained and free-spirited, with a towering frame and great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and unconventional, tall and powerfully built.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，世宗征淮南，福徒步謁見於壽春。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, when the Shizong Emperor campaigned against Huainan, Fu went on foot to present himself at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign of the Later Zhou, when Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Fu walked to Shouchun to seek an audience.

sentences.zh: 世宗奇之，因留麾下。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor regarded him as extraordinary and therefore kept him in his personal following.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by him and kept him in his retinue.

sentences.zh: 每出戰，則令福率衛士為先鋒，與破紫金山砦。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out to battle, he would have Fu lead the bodyguard as vanguard, and together they captured the Zijin Mountain stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he had Fu lead the imperial guards as vanguard; together they took the Zijin Mountain fort.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，錄功授懷德指揮使。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, his merit was recorded and he was appointed commander of the Huaide command.
translations.idiomatic: After Huainan was pacified, his service was recognized with appointment as commander of the Huaide regiment.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷橫海指揮使，率所部隸步帥劉光毅，由峽路征蜀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to commander of the Henghai command, led his troops under the infantry marshal Liu Guangyi, and marched against Shu by the gorge route.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was promoted to commander of the Henghai regiment and led his men under infantry commander Liu Guangyi on the campaign against Shu through the gorges.

sentences.zh: 比至成都，孟昶已降。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Chengdu, Meng Chang had already surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Chengdu, Meng Chang had already submitted.

sentences.zh: 大將王全斌部送降卒歸京師，至綿州，降卒盜庫兵，劫蜀舊將全師雄以叛，焚廬舍，剽財貨以去。

translations.literal: The great general Wang Quanbin was escorting surrendered troops back to the capital; at Mianzhou the surrendered troops stole weapons from the arsenal, seized the former Shu general Quan Shixiong to lead a revolt, burned dwellings, and plundered goods before departing.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Quanbin was escorting surrendered troops to the capital when, at Mianzhou, the captives raided the armory, forced the former Shu officer Quan Shixiong to lead a rebellion, burned buildings, and looted property as they fled.

sentences.zh: 刺史成彥饒以同、華兵百餘人守其城，全斌遣米光緒將七百騎及福所部以屯護之。

translations.literal: The prefect Cheng Yanrao held the city with a little over a hundred Tong and Hua troops; Quanbin sent Mi Guangxu with seven hundred cavalry and Fu's command to garrison and protect it.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cheng Yanrao held the city with just over a hundred troops from Tong and Hua; Quanbin sent Mi Guangxu with seven hundred horsemen and Fu's unit to reinforce the garrison.

sentences.zh: 光緒盡殺師雄妻孥，師雄領叛卒，益聚村民十餘萬眾，攻城益急。

translations.literal: Guangxu killed all of Shixiong's wife and children; Shixiong led the rebel troops and further gathered more than a hundred thousand villagers, pressing the siege ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu had Shixiong's entire family put to death; Shixiong then led the rebels and rallied more than a hundred thousand local villagers, tightening the siege.

sentences.zh: 會龍捷指揮使田紹斌率精銳百騎，由東山西北行，福領所部由山南行，出賊不意，夾擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the Longjie commander Tian Shaobin led a hundred elite horsemen northwest along the eastern hills, while Fu led his troops south along the mountain, catching the rebels unawares and attacking from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Longjie commander Tian Shaobin meanwhile led a hundred picked horsemen down the eastern hills from the northwest, while Fu advanced from the south—taking the enemy by surprise and striking from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大潰，斬首及溺江死者以萬計，以功授虎捷都虞候。

translations.literal: The rebel masses collapsed in great disorder; those beheaded and drowned in the river numbered in the tens of thousands; for his merit he was appointed chief adjutant of the Hujie command.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel force broke utterly; those killed or drowned in the river ran to tens of thousands. For this feat he was made chief adjutant of the Hujie regiment.

sentences.zh: 繼隸曹彬麾下，平江南。

translations.literal: He then served under Cao Bin and pacified Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Cao Bin in the pacification of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 還，授指揮使，領蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed commander and concurrently prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was made a regiment commander and concurrently prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 從太宗克幷、汾，遷馬步都軍頭、武州團練使。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in the conquest of Bing and Fen, and was transferred to commander-in-chief of horse and foot and regimental commissioner of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Taizong in the capture of Bing and Fen and was promoted to commander-in-chief of cavalry and infantry and regimental commissioner of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，出為洺州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duan Gong era he went out as defense commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Duan Gong reign he was posted as defense commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，改雄州防禦使兼本州兵馬部署。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to defense commissioner of Xiongzhou and concurrently military deployment commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was reassigned as defense commissioner of Xiongzhou and concurrent military deployment commissioner for the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雄州地控邊塞，常屯重兵。

translations.literal: Xiongzhou's territory controlled the frontier passes and regularly quartered heavy forces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhou commanded the frontier and always held a large garrison.

sentences.zh: 福至部，按行城壘，調鎮兵以給繕完，出私錢以資宴犒，寇雖大至，而恃以無恐矣。

translations.literal: When Fu reached his post he inspected the walls and ramparts, deployed garrison troops for repairs, and spent private funds for banquets and rewards; though the enemy came in great force, they relied on this and had no fear.
translations.idiomatic: On taking up his post Fu inspected the fortifications, detailed garrison troops to repairs, and paid for feasts and rewards from his own purse; even when large enemy forces appeared, the defenders felt secure.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，遷涼州觀察使、判雄州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was transferred to observation commissioner of Liangzhou and acting administrator of Xiongzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era he was promoted to observation commissioner of Liangzhou and acting administrator of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 福雖不學，而御下有方略，為政簡易，人甚德之。

translations.literal: Although Fu was unlearned, he had strategy in commanding subordinates, his governance was simple and easy, and the people greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Fu had little formal learning, he commanded his men with shrewdness and governed simply and fairly; the people held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 領雄州五年，郡境寧謐。

translations.literal: He held Xiongzhou for five years, and the commandery's territory was tranquil and secure.
translations.idiomatic: During his five years at Xiongzhou the prefecture remained peaceful.

sentences.zh: 福既貴，諸子嘗勸起大第，福怒曰：「我受祿厚，足以僦舍以庇。

translations.literal: After Fu had risen high, his sons once urged him to build a great mansion; Fu angrily said, "I receive generous salary, enough to rent lodging for shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen high, his sons urged him to build a grand residence. Fu grew angry and said, "My salary is ample enough to rent a house for shelter.

sentences.zh: 汝曹既無尺寸功以報朝廷，豈可營度居室，為自安計乎？」

translations.literal: You have not the slightest merit to repay the court—how can you plan dwellings for your own comfort?"
translations.idiomatic: You have done nothing whatsoever to repay the court—how dare you plan comfortable homes for yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He never allowed it.

sentences.zh: 既死，上聞其言，賜其子白金五千兩，使市第宅。

translations.literal: After his death the emperor heard his words and bestowed on his son five thousand taels of white gold to purchase a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor heard what he had said and granted his son five thousand taels of silver to buy a residence.

sentences.zh: 安守忠

translations.literal: An Shouzhong
translations.idiomatic: An Shouzhong

sentences.zh: 安守忠，字信臣，幷州晉陽人。

translations.literal: An Shouzhong, style Xinchen, was a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Shouzhong, courtesy name Xinchen, was from Jinyang in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父審琦，為周平盧軍節度，封陳王。

translations.literal: His father Shenqi was military commissioner of the Pinglu army under Zhou and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father An Shenqi served as military commissioner of the Pinglu army under the Later Zhou and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 晉天福八年，審琦出領山南東道，以守忠為牙內指揮使，領繡州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu of Jin, Shenqi went out to head Shannan East Circuit, appointing Shouzhong as commander of the inner guard and concurrently prefect of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Later Jin Tianfu era, Shenqi took up command of Shannan East Circuit and made Shouzhong commander of his personal guard, with concurrent appointment as prefect of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 周顯德四年春，改鞍轡庫使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Xiande of Zhou he was changed to commissioner of the saddle and bridle storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth Xiande year of the Later Zhou he was made commissioner of the saddle and bridle depot.

sentences.zh: 會淮南初下，命守忠馳往宣諭。

translations.literal: When Huainan had just been taken, he was ordered to ride swiftly there to proclaim and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan had just been conquered, he was sent posthaste to announce the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 時藩臣驕蹇，遇朝使多簡傲，守忠抗以正禮，無所辱命。

translations.literal: At that time regional lords were arrogant and obstinate, and toward court envoys were often curt and disdainful; Shouzhong opposed them with proper ritual and in no way disgraced his commission.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders were then arrogant and often treated court envoys with disdain; Shouzhong held them to proper protocol and never failed his mission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改衛州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，入為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he entered the capital as general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was recalled to court as general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，湖南初平，命為永州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, when Hunan had just been pacified, he was appointed prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong, after Hunan was pacified, he was appointed prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，護河陰屯兵。

translations.literal: During Qiande he oversaw the garrison troops at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era he commanded the garrison at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，太祖知遠俗苦苛虐，南鄭為走集之地，故特命守忠知興元府以撫綏之。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, Taizu knew that remote customs suffered under harsh oppression, and that Nanzheng was a gathering place for travelers; therefore he specially appointed Shouzhong to administer Xingyuan Prefecture to soothe and settle the region.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was conquered, the Taizu Emperor knew the frontier peoples had suffered harsh rule and that Nanzheng was a major crossroads; he therefore specially appointed Shouzhong prefect of Xingyuan to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 四年，改漢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to prefect of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to prefect of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時寇難甫平，使車旁午，公帑不足，守忠出私錢以給用。

translations.literal: At that time the turmoil of invasion had just been settled, envoys' carriages came one after another, and the public treasury was insufficient; Shouzhong spent private funds to supply needs.
translations.idiomatic: The region had only just been pacified, envoys arrived in constant succession, and the public treasury was bare; Shouzhong met expenses from his own funds.

sentences.zh: 每遣使，太祖必戒之曰：「安守忠在蜀，能律已以正，汝行見之，當效其為人也。」

translations.literal: Whenever he dispatched envoys, Taizu always admonished them, saying, "An Shouzhong in Shu can restrain himself and uphold rectitude; when you go and see him, you should emulate his conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent envoys to the region, Taizu would warn them: "An Shouzhong in Shu disciplines himself and upholds integrity—when you meet him, take him as your model."

sentences.zh: 開寶初，改濮州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao he was changed to prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaibao era he was made prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 會河決澶州，命守忠副潁州團練使曹翰護役，河決遂塞。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Cao Prefecture, he was ordered to assist the regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, Cao Han, in overseeing the works, and the breach was then closed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke its banks at Cao Prefecture, he was ordered to assist Yingzhou regimental commissioner Cao Han in the repair works, and the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 五年，知遼州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made administrator of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed administrator of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 民有陰召幷寇謀內應者，事泄，守忠悉斬以徇。

translations.literal: Among the people were those who secretly summoned Bing enemies to plot internal collusion; when the affair was exposed, Shouzhong had them all beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When civilians were discovered secretly inviting Bingzhou raiders to act as inside collaborators, Shouzhong had them all executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 九年，命將征太原，守忠受詔與孫晏宣由遼州入，既而與路羅砦監押馬繼恩遇，乃相與會兵入賊境，燔砦四十餘，獲牛羊數千。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to campaign against Taiyuan; Shouzhong received the edict and with Sun Yanxuan entered by way of Liaozhou; afterward he met Ma Jien, supervisor of the Luluo stockade, and together they united forces, entered enemy territory, burned more than forty stockades, and captured several thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when troops were ordered against Taiyuan, Shouzhong was directed to enter with Sun Yanxuan through Liaozhou; he then joined Luluo stockade supervisor Ma Jien, and together they raided enemy territory, burning more than forty forts and capturing thousands of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 議將深入，會上崩，乃班師。

translations.literal: They discussed advancing deeper, but the emperor died, and they therefore withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: They were planning a deeper advance when the emperor died, and the army was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，移知靈州，在官凡七年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to administer Lingzhou, holding office altogether seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was transferred to Lingzhou, where he served seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，改知易州，徙夏州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was changed to administer Yizhou and transferred to Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Yongxi year he was reassigned to Yizhou and then to Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 每西戎犯邊，戰無不捷，錄功就拜濮州團練使。

translations.literal: Whenever the western tribes raided the border he was victorious in every battle; his merit was recorded and he was immediately appointed regimental commissioner of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever western tribes raided the frontier he was invariably victorious, and for his record of success he was promptly made regimental commissioner of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，知滄州，改瀛州，兼高陽關駐泊部署，遷瀛州防禦使。

translations.literal: During Duan Gong he administered Cangzhou, was changed to Yingzhou, concurrently served as deployment commissioner garrisoned at Gaoyang Pass, and was promoted to defense commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duan Gong era he governed Cangzhou, then Yingzhou, concurrently as deployment commissioner at Gaoyang Pass, and was promoted to defense commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，守忠嘗夢一「濮」字方丈餘，及領是郡幾二十年，於是始悟。

translations.literal: Earlier Shouzhong had once dreamed of the character "Pu" more than a zhang square; only after he had held that prefecture for nearly twenty years did he now understand.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Shouzhong had dreamed of the character for "Pu" more than ten feet across; only after governing that prefecture for nearly twenty years did he grasp the omen.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，徙知雄州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was transferred to administer Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Chunhua year he was transferred to Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 方與僚佐宴飲，有軍校謀變，擐甲及閽，閽者倉卒入白。

translations.literal: Just as he was feasting with his staff, a military officer plotted mutiny, donned armor, and reached the gate; the gatekeeper rushed in to report.
translations.idiomatic: While he was dining with his staff, an officer plotted mutiny and advanced in armor to the gate; the gatekeeper rushed in to report.

sentences.zh: 守忠言笑自若，徐顧坐客曰：「此輩酒狂爾，擒之可也。」

translations.literal: Shouzhong spoke and laughed as if at ease, slowly turning to the seated guests and saying, "These fellows are merely drunk and wild—seize them and that will do."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong remained calm and smiling, then turned leisurely to his guests and said, "They are merely drunk and unruly—arrest them and that will settle it."

sentences.zh: 人服其量焉。

translations.literal: People admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his composure.

sentences.zh: 明年，加耀州觀察使，兼判雄州。

translations.literal: The next year he was additionally made observation commissioner of Yaozhou and concurrently acting administrator of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was additionally made observation commissioner of Yaozhou and concurrent acting administrator of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾召還，條陳邊事，敷奏稱旨，賜錢五百萬。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled, set forth frontier affairs item by item, and his presentation pleased the emperor, who bestowed five million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to court, where his detailed report on frontier affairs pleased the emperor, who granted him five million in cash.

sentences.zh: 五年，又知滄州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again administered Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again posted to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道初，移雄州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he was moved to Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhidao era he was transferred to Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，復知滄州。

translations.literal: In the third year he again administered Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 拜感德軍節度觀察留後，徙宋州，兼制置營田使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor and observation deputy of Gande Army, transferred to Songzhou, and concurrently made commissioner for organizing military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor and observation deputy of the Gande army, transferred to Songzhou, and concurrently made commissioner for military colonies.

sentences.zh: 威德兼著，吏民不忍其去。

translations.literal: His authority and virtue were both manifest, and officials and people could not bear his departure.
translations.idiomatic: His authority and kindness were equally renowned, and officials and commoners alike were reluctant to see him leave.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年入覲，遣還未行，暴卒，年六十九，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he came to court for audience; he was sent back but had not yet departed when he died suddenly, aged sixty-nine; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he presented himself at court; he was dismissed to return but died suddenly before he could leave, at sixty-nine; he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 錄其子繼昌為供備庫副使，婿王世及為光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: His son Jichang was enrolled as deputy commissioner of the supply and equipment storehouse, and his son-in-law Wang Shiji as vice director of the Imperial Household Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jichang was enrolled as deputy commissioner of the supply depot, and his son-in-law Wang Shiji as vice director of the Imperial Household Office.

sentences.zh: 守忠謹愨淡薄，為治簡靜。

translations.literal: Shouzhong was prudent, sincere, and indifferent to gain; his governance was simple and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong was prudent, sincere, and unassuming; his administration was simple and restrained.

sentences.zh: 太祖居藩日，素相厚善，及受禪後，每優任之，守忠處之益謙。

translations.literal: When Taizu was still in his princely domain they had long been on close and friendly terms; after he received the abdication he always favored Shouzhong with appointments, and Shouzhong became all the more humble in his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He and Taizu had been close friends since the emperor's days as a military governor; after the founding of the dynasty Taizu repeatedly favored him with appointments, and Shouzhong grew only more modest.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，多與謀略，人罕知之者。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Taiyuan he often contributed to strategy, which few people knew.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he often advised on strategy, though few were aware of it.

sentences.zh: 所至藩郡，樂施予，豐宴犒，且喜與士大夫遊從，故時論多與之。

translations.literal: In every frontier prefecture he reached he delighted in giving, lavished feasts and rewards, and enjoyed associating with scholar-officials; therefore contemporary opinion often spoke well of him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he was generous, held lavish feasts for his troops, and enjoyed the company of literati; contemporary opinion generally spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 初，審琦以愛妾故，為隸人所戕。

translations.literal: Earlier Shenqi, on account of a beloved concubine, was killed by a bondservant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenqi had once been murdered by a bondservant over a favored concubine.

sentences.zh: 守忠終身不畜妓妾，而喜佞佛，蓋有所懲云。

translations.literal: Shouzhong throughout his life kept no singing girls or concubines, yet delighted in devotion to Buddhism—perhaps because he had something to take warning from, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong kept no concubines all his life and favored Buddhist devotion—perhaps, it is said, as a lesson drawn from that tragedy.

sentences.zh: 孔守正

translations.literal: Kong Shouzheng
translations.idiomatic: Kong Shouzheng

sentences.zh: 孔守正，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: Kong Shouzheng was a native of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Shouzheng was from Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 幼事後唐明宗子許王從益。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Later Tang Mingzong's son, Prince Xu, Congyi.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served Prince Xu Congyi, son of Later Tang Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 漢初，為東西班承旨，事魏王承訓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was an attendant of the eastern and western classes and served Prince Wei, Chengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han he was an attendant of the eastern and western palace guards and served Prince Wei Chengxun.

sentences.zh: 周世宗征淮南，以材勇選為東班承旨。

translations.literal: When the Zhou Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he was selected for talent and courage as eastern-class attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhou Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he was chosen for his talent and valor as eastern-class attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋初，補內殿直，兼領驍雄、吐渾指揮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was appointed inner palace guard and concurrently led the Xiaoxiong and Tuhun commands.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made an inner palace guard and concurrently commanded the Xiaoxiong and Tuhun regiments.

sentences.zh: 從劉廷翰平蜀，還，遷驍雄副指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Liu Tinghan in pacifying Shu; on his return he was promoted to deputy commander of Xiaoxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Liu Tinghan in the conquest of Shu and, on returning, was promoted to deputy commander of the Xiaoxiong regiment.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，太祖征太原，守正隸何繼筠麾下。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, when Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan, Shouzheng served under He Jiyun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era, when Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan, Shouzheng served under He Jiyun.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣兵來援晉陽，守正接戰於石嶺關，大敗之，斬首萬級，獲其將王破得。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent troops to relieve Jinyang, Shouzheng engaged them at Shiling Pass, routed them utterly, beheaded ten thousand ranks, and captured their general Wang Pode.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan sent troops to relieve Jinyang, Shouzheng met them at Shiling Pass, inflicted a crushing defeat, took ten thousand heads, and captured their general Wang Pode.

sentences.zh: 時宋師之陷敵者數百人，守正以騎軍馳之，盡奪以還。

translations.literal: At that time several hundred Song troops had fallen into the enemy's hands; Shouzheng charged with cavalry and recovered them all.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Song soldiers had been captured; Shouzheng charged with his cavalry and rescued them all.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，累遷日騎東西班指揮使。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he was repeatedly promoted to commander of the eastern and western Riji classes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he rose through successive promotions to commander of the eastern and western Riji guards.

sentences.zh: 太宗親征晉陽，守正分主城西洞屋，領步卒大呼先登，繼與內侍蔡守恩等率騎兵力戰，晉軍遂潰。

translations.literal: When Taizong personally campaigned against Jinyang, Shouzheng was assigned the western siege towers at the city wall; leading infantry he shouted and was first to ascend, then together with the inner attendant Cai Shouen and others led cavalry in fierce battle, and the Jin army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong personally besieged Jinyang, Shouzheng commanded the western assault towers; leading infantry he was first over the wall with a great shout, then with the eunuch Cai Shouen and others led the cavalry in fierce fighting until the Jin army broke.

sentences.zh: 從征范陽，至金臺驛，詔與劉仁蘊先趨岐溝關。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Fanyang, when they reached Jintai Post Station, he was ordered with Liu Renyun to hurry ahead to Qigou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the Fanyang campaign, at Jintai Post Station he was ordered with Liu Renyun to press ahead to Qigou Pass.

sentences.zh: 時城未下，守正夜超垣，度鹿角，臨機橋，以大軍將至，說關使劉禹使降。

translations.literal: The city had not yet fallen; Shouzheng by night scaled the wall, crossed the abatis, reached the drawbridge, and with the great army about to arrive persuaded the pass commissioner Liu Yu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The city had not yet fallen; Shouzheng scaled the wall by night, crossed the abatis, reached the drawbridge, and persuaded pass commissioner Liu Yu to surrender by warning that the main army was near.

sentences.zh: 禹解懸橋，守正遂入城，撫諭其軍民，以城守屬綦廷朗，而已赴行在。

translations.literal: Yu lowered the drawbridge; Shouzheng then entered the city, soothed and instructed its troops and people, entrusted defense of the city to Qi Tinglang, and himself proceeded to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yu lowered the drawbridge; Shouzheng entered, reassured the troops and populace, left the city under Qi Tinglang, and himself hurried to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 時契丹兵在涿州東，守正與傅潛率御前東西班分兩陣馳擊之，逐北二十餘里，降其羽林兵數百人。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan troops were east of Zhuozhou; Shouzheng and Fu Qian led the eastern and western imperial guards in two formations charging to attack, pursued them north more than twenty li, and accepted the surrender of several hundred Yulin troops.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan forces were then east of Zhuozhou; Shouzheng and Fu Qian led the eastern and western imperial guards in a two-pronged charge, pursued them more than twenty li, and accepted the surrender of several hundred Yulin guards.

sentences.zh: 繼與高懷德、劉廷翰合兵追之至桑乾河，契丹自是不敢近塞。

translations.literal: He then united forces with Gao Huaide and Liu Tinghan in pursuit to the Sanggan River, and thereafter the Khitan did not dare approach the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Gao Huaide and Liu Tinghan in pursuit to the Sanggan River, after which the Khitan no longer dared approach the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 以勞再遷日騎都指揮使，領濡州刺史。

translations.literal: For his labors he was again promoted to commander of Riji and concurrently prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was again promoted to commander of the Riji guard and concurrently prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷龍衛都指揮使，領長州團練使，出鎮真定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was transferred to commander of Longwei, concurrently regimental commissioner of Changzhou, and went out to garrison Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Duan Gong era he was made commander of the Longwei guard and regimental commissioner of Changzhou, and posted to garrison Zhending.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，出為潁州防禦使。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as defense commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was posted as defense commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太宗以其練習戎旅，特置龍衛、神衛四廂都指揮使以授之。

translations.literal: Before long Taizong, because of his mastery of military affairs, specially created the four-division commanders of Longwei and Shenwei and invested him with the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Taizong, recognizing his mastery of military affairs, specially created the four-division commands of Longwei and Shenwei and appointed him to lead them.

sentences.zh: 改領振州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was changed to concurrently defense commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently made defense commissioner of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜殿前都虞候，領容州觀察使。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 一日，侍宴北苑，上入玄武門，守正大醉，與王榮論邊功於駕前，忿爭失儀，侍臣請以屬吏，上弗許。

translations.literal: One day, while attending a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor entered the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng was greatly drunk and with Wang Rong disputed frontier merit before the imperial carriage, quarreling in anger and losing propriety; attendants asked that they be handed to the judicial officers, but the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: One day at a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor passed through the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng, very drunk, argued with Wang Rong over frontier exploits before the imperial carriage, quarreling loudly and forgetting decorum; attendants asked that they be turned over to the judicial authorities, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 翌日，俱詣殿廷請罪，上曰：「朕亦大醉，漫不復省。」

translations.literal: The next day they both came to the palace hall to plead guilty; the emperor said, "I too was greatly drunk and scarcely remember it."
translations.idiomatic: The next day both came to court to apologize; the emperor said, "I was drunk myself and scarcely remember it."

sentences.zh: 遂釋不問。

translations.literal: He then released them without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the matter without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 俄命為定州行營副部署，受詔詣保州軍開道，遇敵於曹河，與戰數合，梟首三十餘，獲馬五十匹，上聞而壯之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed deputy commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters, received an edict to proceed to Ba prefecture army to open a route, encountered the enemy at Cao River, fought several engagements, took more than thirty heads, captured fifty horses; when the emperor heard of it he applauded his valor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made deputy commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters and, by imperial order, sent to Ba prefecture to open a route. At Cao River he met the enemy and fought several engagements, taking more than thirty heads and fifty horses. When the emperor heard the report, he praised his martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，擢高陽關副都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was promoted to deputy overall commander of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chunhua era he was promoted to deputy overall commander of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 軍中小將有詈其校長者，守正械送闕下，取裁於上，未嘗專決焉。

translations.literal: When a junior officer in the army cursed his company commander, Shouzheng had him put in fetters and sent to the capital for the emperor's judgment, never deciding such matters on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: When a junior officer in the ranks cursed his company commander, Shouzheng had him shackled and sent to court for the emperor's decision, never ruling on such cases by his own authority.

sentences.zh: 明年，護浚惠民河，塞澶州決河，就命知州軍。

translations.literal: The next year he supervised dredging of the Huimin Canal and blocking the breach in the Yellow River at Cao prefecture, and was concurrently appointed military governor of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he oversaw dredging of the Huimin Canal and closing the Yellow River breach at Cao prefecture, and was concurrently appointed military governor there.

sentences.zh: 改慎州觀察使，還，領代州部署，連移幷代、夏綏、麟府三鎮。

translations.literal: He was made observation commissioner of Shen prefecture; upon returning he took command as overall commissioner of Dai prefecture, and in succession was transferred among the three garrison commands of Bing-Dai, Xia-Sui, and Lin-Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Shen prefecture, then upon returning took overall command at Dai prefecture and was transferred in turn among the three frontier commands of Bing-Dai, Xia-Sui, and Lin-Fu.

sentences.zh: 與李繼遷戰大橫岡，援范廷召出塞，破賊於白池，至行莊，焚掠甚眾，改代、夏二州部署。

translations.literal: He fought Li Jiqian at Dahenggang, relieved Fan Tingzhao beyond the frontier, defeated the rebels at Baichi, reached Xingzhuang, and burned and plundered extensively; he was made overall commissioner of Dai and Xia prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Li Jiqian at Dahenggang, relieved Fan Tingzhao beyond the passes, routed the rebels at Baichi, and pushed on to Xingzhuang, where his forces burned and plundered on a large scale. He was then made overall commissioner of Dai and Xia prefectures.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，復徙代州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, he was again transferred to Dai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne, he was again posted to Dai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，授昌化軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was granted the post of military governor and observer of Changhua Army with the title of interim regent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xianping era he was granted the post of military governor and observer of Changhua Army as interim regent.

sentences.zh: 守正上言：「四任雁門，邊亭久安，願徙東北以自效。」

translations.literal: Shouzheng memorialized: "Having held four appointments at Yanmen, where the frontier posts have long been at peace, I wish to be transferred to the northeast to prove my worth."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzheng memorialized: "I have served four terms at Yanmen, where the frontier has long been quiet. I wish to be transferred to the northeast to prove my worth."

sentences.zh: 會夏人入寇，改定州行營副都部署。

translations.literal: Just then the Tangut raided, and he was changed to deputy overall commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Tangut invaded, and he was reassigned as deputy overall commander of the Dingzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四年，移彰德軍留後，以風疾妨政，改安化軍留後。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to regent of Zhangde Army; as wind affliction hindered his administration, he was changed to regent of Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to regent of Zhangde Army, but as wind sickness interfered with his duties he was moved to regent of Anhua Army.

sentences.zh: 景德初，復以不任職代。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was again replaced for inability to perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingde era he was again replaced on grounds that he could no longer perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 時議防秋北鄙，守正猶屢表請行。

translations.literal: When deliberations turned to autumn defense of the northern frontier, Shouzheng still repeatedly submitted memorials asking to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated autumn defense of the northern frontier, Shouzheng still repeatedly memorialized asking to take the field.

sentences.zh: 上閔之，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on him and did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him and refused.

sentences.zh: 無何，卒，年六十六，贈泰寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at age sixty-six; posthumously he was granted the post of military governor of Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-six. Posthumously he was granted the post of military governor of Taining Army.

sentences.zh: 譚延美

translations.literal: Tan Yanmei
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yanmei

sentences.zh: 譚延美，大名朝城人。

translations.literal: Tan Yanmei was a native of Chaocheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yanmei was from Chaocheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 軀幹壯偉。

translations.literal: His frame was tall and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He had a tall, powerful build.

sentences.zh: 少不逞，遇群盜聚謀將行剽劫，延美即趨就之。

translations.literal: In youth he was unruly; once when he met a band of robbers gathered to plan a raid, Yanmei immediately went over to join them.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was wild and unrestrained. Once when he came upon a band of robbers gathered to plan a raid, Yanmei immediately went over to join them.

sentences.zh: 及就捕，法皆抵死，延美以與盜素不相識，獲免。

translations.literal: When they were arrested, by law all were liable to death; Yanmei, because he had never known the robbers before, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When they were captured, the law called for death for all of them, but Yanmei was spared because he had never known the robbers before.

sentences.zh: 自後往來澶、魏間，為盜於鄉里，鄉里患之。

translations.literal: Afterward he traveled back and forth between Cao and Wei, robbing in the countryside, to the distress of the local people.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he traveled back and forth between Cao and Wei, robbing in the countryside until the local people were driven to despair.

sentences.zh: 周世宗鎮澶淵，募置帳下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou held Chanyuan, Yanmei was recruited and placed in his personal retinue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou was stationed at Chanyuan, Yanmei was recruited into his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 即位，補殿前散都頭。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded, Yanmei was appointed chief of the Palace Front scattered company.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne, Yanmei was appointed chief of the Palace Front scattered company.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，以勞遷控鶴軍副指揮使。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Huainan, he was promoted for his labors to deputy commander of the Crane-Control Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huainan campaign he was promoted for his service to deputy commander of the Crane-Control Army.

sentences.zh: 又從克三關。

translations.literal: He also followed in the capture of the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the capture of the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 時太祖領禁兵，留督牙隊。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu commanded the palace troops and remained to oversee the guard formation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizu commanded the palace troops and remained behind to oversee the guard formation.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，補控鶴指揮使，稍遷都虞候、馬步副都軍頭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong he was appointed commander of the Crane-Control Army, and gradually rose to chief adjutant and deputy commander-in-chief of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianlong he was made commander of the Crane-Control Army and gradually rose to chief adjutant and deputy commander-in-chief of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 征湖南，與解暉分領行營戰棹都指揮使。

translations.literal: On the Hunan campaign he shared command of the field fleet with Xie Hui as co-commanders of the battle-ship forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the Hunan campaign he and Xie Hui jointly commanded the field battle-fleet.

sentences.zh: 時汪端寇攻朗州甚急，招討慕容延釗遣延美率兵赴之，大敗賊眾，擒端以還。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel Wang Duan was pressing Lang prefecture hard; pacification commissioner Murong Yanzhao dispatched Yanmei to lead troops to the relief, routed the rebel host, captured Duan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel Wang Duan was pressing Lang prefecture hard. Pacification commissioner Murong Yanzhao sent Yanmei with troops to the relief, routed the rebel force, captured Duan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 擢鐵騎副指揮使，領睦州刺史，四遷至內殿直都知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Iron Cavalry, concurrently prefect of Mu prefecture, and after four transfers reached director of the Inner Palace Direct.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Iron Cavalry and concurrently made prefect of Mu prefecture, and after four further transfers reached director of the Inner Palace Direct.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，為蘄州刺史，連徙廬、壽、濠、光州軍巡檢使，劇賊之為害者悉就捕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was prefect of Qi prefecture, then in succession prefecture-and-army inspector of Lu, Shou, Hao, and Guang; all the most dangerous bandits were captured.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taiping Xingguo era he was made prefect of Qi prefecture, then served in succession as prefecture-and-army inspector of Lu, Shou, Hao, and Guang, capturing every major bandit who had been plaguing the region.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙知威虜軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to command Weilu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to command Weilu Army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，舉兵北伐，命延美為幽州西面行營都監，與田重進出飛狐北。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi the court raised troops for the northern expedition; Yanmei was appointed chief overseer of the western field headquarters at You prefecture, and with Tian Chongjin advanced north of Feihu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi the court launched a northern expedition. Yanmei was appointed chief overseer of the western field headquarters at You prefecture and, with Tian Chongjin, advanced north of Feihu.

sentences.zh: 俄遇敵，延美曰：「彼恃眾易我，宜出其不意先攻之。」

translations.literal: Soon they met the enemy; Yanmei said: "They rely on numbers to take us lightly; we should strike first when they do not expect it."
translations.idiomatic: Soon they met the enemy. Yanmei said: "They rely on their numbers and take us lightly. We should strike first while they do not expect it."

sentences.zh: 即麾騎軍直進，敵兵將潰，大軍繼至，遂敗之，斬首五百，獲其將大鵬翼以獻，以功擢本州防禦使。

translations.literal: He immediately directed the cavalry straight forward; the enemy was on the verge of collapse when the main army arrived, and they were defeated; five hundred heads were taken, and the enemy general Dapeng Yi was captured and presented; for his merit he was promoted to defense commissioner of the local prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately led the cavalry straight forward. The enemy was on the verge of breaking when the main army arrived, and they were routed. Five hundred heads were taken, and the enemy general Dapeng Yi was captured and presented. For his merit he was promoted to defense commissioner of the local prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改亳州，出為鎮州鈐轄。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Bo prefecture and sent out as supervisory commissioner of Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Bo prefecture and sent out as supervisory commissioner of Zhen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，徙知寧遠軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong he was transferred to command Ningyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duangong (988) he was transferred to command Ningyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 一旦，契丹兵抵城下，延美開門以示之，不敢入。

translations.literal: One day Khitan troops reached the city walls; Yanmei opened the gates to show them and they did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: One day Khitan troops reached the city walls. Yanmei opened the gates to show them, and they did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 圍城數日，開門如故，民出取芻糧者無異平日，契丹卒疑之，遂引去。

translations.literal: After besieging the city for several days with the gates still open as before, and the people going out to gather fodder and grain no differently than on ordinary days, the Khitan soldiers grew suspicious and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After besieging the city for several days with the gates still open as before, and the people going out to gather fodder and grain no differently than on ordinary days, the Khitan soldiers grew suspicious and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二年，進邕州觀察使、判亳州，兼知代州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to observation commissioner of Yong prefecture and acting prefect of Bo prefecture, concurrently governing Dai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to observation commissioner of Yong prefecture and acting prefect of Bo prefecture, while also governing Dai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是時任邊郡者，皆令兼領內地一州，處其家屬。

translations.literal: At that time those appointed to frontier prefectures were all ordered to concurrently hold an interior prefecture to house their families.
translations.idiomatic: At that time officials assigned to frontier prefectures were all ordered to concurrently hold an interior prefecture where their families could reside.

sentences.zh: 徙知潞、陝、涇州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Lu, Shan, and Jing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Lu, Shan, and Jing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，以左領軍衛上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he retired as senior general of the Left Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping (1001) he retired as senior general of the Left Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年八十三，贈建武軍節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged eighty-three, and was posthumously granted the post of military governor of the Jianwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, aged eighty-three, and was posthumously granted the title of military governor of the Jianwu army.

sentences.zh: 子繼倫，至崇儀副使；

translations.literal: His son Jilun rose to deputy commissioner of honored ritual;
translations.idiomatic: His son Jilun rose to deputy commissioner of honored ritual;

sentences.zh: 雍，虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Yong was an outer-office member of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was an outer-office member of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 元達，初名守旻，洺州雞澤人。

translations.literal: Yuan Da — originally named Shoumin — was a native of Jize in Ming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Da, originally named Shoumin, was from Jize in Ming prefecture.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺餘，負膂力，善射。

translations.literal: More than eight feet tall, endowed with strength of back, skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than eight feet tall, possessed great strength, and was skilled at archery.

sentences.zh: 家業農，不任作苦，委耒耜，慨歎而去之。

translations.literal: His family livelihood was farming; unable to endure hard labor, he cast aside plow and hoe, sighed, and left.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived by farming, but unable to bear hard labor he cast aside plow and hoe, sighed, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 事任俠，縱酒。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to chivalrous deeds and drank freely.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to chivalrous deeds and drank to excess.

sentences.zh: 嘗醉，見道旁槐樹，拔劍斬之，樹立斷。

translations.literal: Once when drunk he saw a pagoda tree by the roadside, drew his sword and struck it, and the tree severed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once when drunk he saw a pagoda tree by the roadside, drew his sword and struck it, and the tree split clean through.

sentences.zh: 達私喜曰：「吾聞李將軍射石虎飲羽，今樹為我斷，豈神助歟？」

translations.literal: Da said privately in delight: "I have heard that General Li shot an arrow into a stone tiger until the shaft sank in; now the tree breaks for me — is this divine aid?"
translations.idiomatic: Da said privately, delighted: "I have heard that General Li drove an arrow into a stone tiger until the shaft sank in. Now a tree breaks for me — is this the gods lending their aid?"

sentences.zh: 嘗從少年數十百人欲起為盜，里中父老交戒之，乃止。

translations.literal: He once intended to take several dozen or hundred young men and rise as bandits, but the village elders jointly warned him, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Once he gathered several dozen or hundred young men intending to take to banditry, but the village elders jointly warned him, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 時郡以戶籍調役，達當送徒闕下，行數舍，乃悉縱之，曰：「吾觀汝曹，亦丈夫也，豈樂為是哉？

translations.literal: At the time the prefecture was assigning corvée labor by household registers; Da was obliged to escort conscript laborers to the capital; after traveling several stops he released them all, saying: "I see that you too are true men — would you take pleasure in this?
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prefecture was assigning corvée labor by household registers. Da was obliged to escort conscript laborers to the capital, but after traveling several stops he released them all, saying: "I see that you too are true men. Would you take pleasure in this?

sentences.zh: 可善自為計，吾亦從此逝矣！」

translations.literal: Make good plans for yourselves; I too shall depart from here!"
translations.idiomatic: Make good plans for yourselves. I too shall depart from here!"

sentences.zh: 已而郡遣追捕，至則達援弓引滿待之，追者不敢近。

translations.literal: Before long the prefecture sent pursuers; when they arrived Da strung his bow and drew it full, waiting for them, and the pursuers did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the prefecture sent pursuers. When they arrived Da strung his bow and drew it full, waiting for them, and the pursuers did not dare come near.

sentences.zh: 由是亡命山林間，為鄉里患。

translations.literal: Thereafter he became an outlaw in the mountains and forests, a scourge to the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he became an outlaw in the mountains and forests, a scourge to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 太宗居晉邸時，達求見，得隸帳下。

translations.literal: When Taizong resided at the Prince of Jin establishment, Da sought an audience and was enrolled in his personal retinue.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong resided at the Prince of Jin establishment, Da sought an audience and was enrolled in his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍太宗習射園亭，命之射，達射四發不中的，已而連中。

translations.literal: Once while attending Taizong practicing archery in a garden pavilion, he was ordered to shoot; Da fired four arrows without hitting, then hit in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending Taizong practicing archery in a garden pavilion, he was ordered to shoot. Da fired four arrows without hitting, then hit in succession.

sentences.zh: 上喜，為更其名曰達。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and changed his given name to Da.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and changed his given name to Da.

sentences.zh: 及即位，補御龍直隊長。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, Da was appointed captain of the Imperial Dragon Direct company.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Da was appointed captain of the Imperial Dragon Direct company.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，累遷媯州刺史，繼領本州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Guizhou and then concurrently held regimental commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi era he rose to prefect of Guizhou and then concurrently served as regimental commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進州郡部送亡命者至闕，左右諷殺之，達奏曰：「此類竄匿者眾，豈能盡殺之哉？

translations.literal: When fugitives escorted by prefecture and county authorities reached the capital, attendants hinted that they should be killed. Da memorialized: "Fugitives of this kind who hide in the wild are many—how could we kill them all?
translations.idiomatic: When fugitives escorted by prefecture and county authorities reached the capital, attendants hinted that they should be killed. Da memorialized: "Fugitives of this kind who hide in the wild are many—how could we kill them all?

sentences.zh: 不如赦之，以開其自新之路，且以成好生之德。」

translations.literal: It would be better to pardon them, to open a path for their own reform, and to fulfill the virtue of cherishing life."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to pardon them, to open a path for their own reform, and to fulfill the virtue of cherishing life."

sentences.zh: 上悅，因悉原之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and therefore pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，擢侍衛步軍都虞候，領幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong he was promoted to chief adjutant of the Palace Guard infantry and made prefect of You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong (989) he was promoted to chief adjutant of the Palace Guard infantry and made prefect of You prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷北面行營都部署，由常山鎮入為京城巡檢。

translations.literal: He served as overall deployment commissioner of the northern field headquarters, then entered the capital from Changshan town as capital patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He served as overall deployment commissioner of the northern field headquarters, then entered the capital from Changshan town as capital patrol inspector.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年卒，年四十二，贈昭化軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he died, aged forty-two, and was posthumously granted the post of military governor of the Zhaohua army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Chunhua (993), aged forty-two, and was posthumously granted the title of military governor of the Zhaohua army.

sentences.zh: 達雖奮自草野，歷職戎署，至交士夫，能折節盡禮，人以是稱之。

translations.literal: Though Da had risen vigorously from the wilds, when he passed through military bureaus and came to know scholar-officials, he could restrain himself and observe full propriety, for which people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Da had risen vigorously from the wilds, once he entered military service and came to know scholar-officials, he could restrain himself and observe full propriety, for which people praised him.

sentences.zh: 常思德

translations.literal: Chang Side
translations.idiomatic: Chang Side

sentences.zh: 常思德，開封人。

translations.literal: Chang Side was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Side was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，以材勇應募，隸天武軍，累遷神衛都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande in Zhou, he volunteered for his talent and bravery, was assigned to the Tianwu Army, and rose through successive transfers to chief adjutant of the Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiande era under Zhou, he volunteered for his talent and bravery, was assigned to the Tianwu Army, and rose through successive transfers to chief adjutant of the Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，從曹彬征幽州，因署牙校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he followed Cao Bin on the Youzhou expedition and was appointed to the guard staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongxi era he followed Cao Bin on the Youzhou expedition and was appointed to the guard staff.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮威虜軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was stationed at Weilu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted to Weilu Army.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，以弓箭直都虞候領溪州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong he was chief adjutant of the Archers Direct, concurrently prefect of Xi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Duan Gong era he was chief adjutant of the Archers Direct and concurrently prefect of Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，李順叛蜀，命往夔、峽招捕，師次達州新寧縣，調近州土兵掩殺賊徒三千餘人於梁山。

translations.literal: In Chunhua, when Li Shun rebelled in Shu, he was ordered to Kuizhou and the Gorges to hunt down rebels; his force halted at Xingning county in Da prefecture; he mobilized local militia from nearby prefectures and at Liangshan ambushed and killed more than three thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, when Li Shun rebelled in Shu, he was ordered to Kuizhou and the Gorges to hunt down rebels. His force halted at Xingning county in Da prefecture, where he mobilized local militia from nearby prefectures and at Liangshan ambushed and killed more than three thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 時雷有終領大軍抵合州境上，賊眾二萬來拒。

translations.literal: At that time Lei Youzhong was leading the main army to the border of He prefecture, and twenty thousand rebels came to oppose.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lei Youzhong was leading the main army to the border of He prefecture, where twenty thousand rebels came out to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 思德與尹元、裴莊等合擊之，合州遂平。

translations.literal: Side, with Yin Yuan, Pei Zhuang, and others jointly attacked them, and He prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Side, with Yin Yuan, Pei Zhuang, and others, jointly attacked them, and He prefecture was pacified.

sentences.zh: 賊帥田奉正、蘇榮據果州，思德因其遁而追捕之，斬首八百。

translations.literal: The rebel chiefs Tian Fengzheng and Su Rong held Guo prefecture; Side pursued them as they fled, taking eight hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chiefs Tian Fengzheng and Su Rong held Guo prefecture. Side pursued them as they fled and took eight hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 果州既定，餘賊保渠州，及走廣安、梁山。

translations.literal: Once Guo prefecture was settled, the remaining rebels held out at Qu prefecture and fled toward Guang'an and Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guo prefecture was settled, the remaining rebels held out at Qu prefecture and fled toward Guang'an and Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵為二：抵廣安、梁山者，思德領之；

translations.literal: He then divided his force in two: Side led those going to Guang'an and Liangshan;
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his force in two: Side led those going to Guang'an and Liangshan;

sentences.zh: 趣渠州者，元、莊領之。

translations.literal: those pressing Qu prefecture were led by Yuan and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: those pressing Qu prefecture were led by Yuan and Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 合力進討，盡殲其黨。

translations.literal: Advancing together in combined attack, the rebel bands were entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing together in a combined attack, they destroyed the rebel bands entirely.

sentences.zh: 自是川、峽賴以安靜，無復寇患，以功真授汝州刺史。

translations.literal: From then on Chuan and the Gorges relied on this for tranquility and had no further raiding troubles; for his merit he was formally invested as prefect of Ru prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Sichuan and the Gorges enjoyed peace and were free of further raids. For his merit he was formally invested as prefect of Ru prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，曹彬北征不利，至涿州，左右皆潰散，獨思德以所部護至易州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cao Bin's northern expedition fared ill, at Zhuo prefecture his attendants all scattered; Side alone with his command escorted him to Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cao Bin's northern expedition fared badly, at Zhuo prefecture his attendants all scattered. Side alone escorted him with his own command as far as Yi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 語人曰：「既備戎行，則與主帥同死生可也。

translations.literal: He told others: "Once one takes the field, one should share life and death with the commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: He told others: "Once one takes the field, one should share life and death with the commanding general.

sentences.zh: 若視利害以為去就，將何面目以見君父乎？」

translations.literal: If one weighs advantage and disadvantage in deciding whether to stay or go, with what face can one appear before lord and father?"
translations.idiomatic: If one weighs advantage and disadvantage in deciding whether to stay or go, with what face can one appear before lord and father?"

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗聞其言，至是陛辭，深加慰勞，且諭之曰：「為臣以忠實為本，汝少壯時，既以驍勇自效，且能盡心於主將，事朕之日雖久，而忠實如一。

translations.literal: Taizong had once heard these words; at this farewell audience he greatly comforted and rewarded him, and instructed him: "Serving as minister, fidelity is the root; in your youth you proved yourself by martial valor, and you devoted your heart to your commander; though you have served Us long, your fidelity has been the same throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had once heard these words. At this farewell audience he greatly comforted and rewarded him, and instructed him: "Serving as minister, fidelity is the foundation. In your youth you proved yourself by martial valor and devoted your heart to your commander. Though you have served Us long, your fidelity has been the same throughout.

sentences.zh: 今雖老，亦當盡心乃職，庶無負乎朕之委寄也。」

translations.literal: Though you are now old, you should still give your full heart to your duties, so as not to betray Our trust."
translations.idiomatic: Though you are now old, you should still give your full heart to your duties, so as not to betray Our trust."

sentences.zh: 未幾，移慶州路副都部署、屯邠州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to deputy overall commander of the Qingzhou circuit and garrisoned Bin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to deputy overall commander of the Qingzhou circuit and garrisoned at Bin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，與李繼隆同部芻糧赴靈州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he joined Li Jilong in escorting forage to Ling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xianping era he joined Li Jilong in escorting forage to Ling prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以疾改陳留都監，換左神武大將軍。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was made supervisory commissioner of Chenliu and exchanged for Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was made supervisory commissioner of Chenliu and exchanged his post for Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 尹繼倫

translations.literal: Yin Jilun
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jilun

sentences.zh: 尹繼倫，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: Yin Jilun was a native of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jilun was from Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父勳，郢州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Xun was defense commissioner of Ying prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun was defense commissioner of Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗內舉繼倫以為可用，太祖以補殿直，權領虎捷指揮，預平嶺表，下金陵。

translations.literal: He once recommended Jilun internally as capable; Taizu appointed him to the Palace Attendant rank, with provisional command of the Tiger Brave Army, and he participated in pacifying Lingnan and capturing Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Jilun internally as capable. Taizu appointed him to the Palace Attendant rank with provisional command of the Tiger Brave Army, and he took part in pacifying Lingnan and capturing Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，改供奉官。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was made palace supply officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, he was made palace supply officer.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，還，遷洛苑使，充北面緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Taiyuan, upon return he was promoted to Luoyang Park commissioner and appointed overall frontier inspector of the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Taiyuan he returned and was promoted to Luoyang Park commissioner and appointed overall frontier inspector of the northern border.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，威虜軍糧饋不繼，契丹潛議入寇。

translations.literal: In the Duan Gong era supplies to Weilu Army were cut off, and the Khitan secretly planned an incursion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duan Gong era supplies to Weilu Army ran short, and the Khitan secretly planned an incursion.

sentences.zh: 上聞，遣李繼隆發鎮、定兵萬餘，護送輜重數千乘。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he dispatched Li Jilong to mobilize more than ten thousand troops from Zhen and Ding to escort several thousand supply wagons.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he dispatched Li Jilong to mobilize more than ten thousand troops from Zhen and Ding to escort several thousand supply wagons.

sentences.zh: 契丹將於越諜知之，率精銳數萬騎，將邀於路。

translations.literal: The Khitan general Yelu Yuyue learned of this through spies and led several tens of thousands of elite cavalry intending to intercept them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan general Yelu Yuyue learned of this through spies and led several tens of thousands of elite cavalry intending to intercept them on the road.

sentences.zh: 繼倫適領兵巡徼，路與寇直。

translations.literal: Jilun happened to be leading troops on patrol when his route directly met the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun happened to be leading troops on patrol when his route ran directly into the raiders.

sentences.zh: 於越徑趨大軍，過繼倫軍，不顧而去。

translations.literal: Yuyue pressed straight toward the main army, passed Jilun's force without regard, and went on.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyue pressed straight toward the main Song army, passed Jilun's force without a glance, and went on.

sentences.zh: 繼倫謂其麾下曰：「寇蔑視我爾。

translations.literal: Jilun said to his officers: "The enemy despises us utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun said to his officers: "The enemy despises us utterly.

sentences.zh: 彼南出而捷，還則乘勝驅我而北，不捷亦且泄怒於我，將無遺類矣。

translations.literal: If they win a quick victory to the south, on their return they will drive us north in triumph; even if they fail they will still vent their rage upon us, and not one of us will survive.
translations.idiomatic: If they win a quick victory to the south, on their return they will drive us north in triumph. Even if they fail they will still vent their rage upon us, and not one of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，但當卷甲銜枚以躡之。

translations.literal: For today the best course is to wrap armor and take the bit between our teeth, then follow in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: For today the best course is to wrap our armor, take the bit between our teeth, and follow in their tracks.

sentences.zh: 彼銳氣前趣，不虞我之至，力戰而勝，足以自樹。

translations.literal: With their fighting spirit rushing forward, they will not expect our arrival; if we fight hard and win, that is enough to establish our fame.
translations.idiomatic: With their fighting spirit rushing forward, they will not expect our arrival. If we fight hard and win, that is enough to establish our fame.

sentences.zh: 縱死猶不失為忠義，豈可泯然而死，為胡地鬼乎！」

translations.literal: Even if we die we shall not fall short of loyalty and righteousness — how can we die in obscurity and become ghosts in barbarian lands!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if we die we shall not fall short of loyalty and righteousness. How can we die in obscurity and become ghosts in barbarian lands!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆憤激從命。

translations.literal: All were indignant and aroused, and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: All were stirred to indignation and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 繼倫令軍中秣馬，俟夜，人持短兵，潛躡其後。

translations.literal: Jilun ordered the army to feed their horses; at night each man took a short weapon and secretly followed in their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun ordered the army to feed their horses. At night each man took a short weapon and secretly followed in their rear.

sentences.zh: 行數十里，至唐河、徐河間。

translations.literal: After traveling several tens of li they reached the country between the Tang and Xu Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: After traveling several tens of li they reached the country between the Tang and Xu Rivers.

sentences.zh: 天未明，越去大軍四五里，會食訖將戰，繼隆方陣於前以待，繼倫從後急擊，殺其將皮室一人。

translations.literal: Before dawn, Yuyue was four or five li from the main army; having finished eating they were about to fight; Jilong had just formed his battle line in front to wait; Jilun struck fiercely from the rear and killed the Khitan general Pishi.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn Yuyue was four or five li from the main Song army. Having finished eating, the Khitan were about to give battle. Jilong had just formed his battle line in front to wait when Jilun struck fiercely from the rear and killed the Khitan general Pishi.

sentences.zh: 皮室者，契丹相也。

translations.literal: Pishi was a chancellor of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Pishi was a chancellor of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 皮室既擒，眾遂驚潰。

translations.literal: Once Pishi had been taken, the host panicked and broke.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pishi had been taken, the Khitan host panicked and broke.

sentences.zh: 於越方食，失箸，為短兵中其臂，創甚，乘善馬先遁。

translations.literal: Yuyue was eating; startled, he dropped his chopsticks, was struck in the arm by a short weapon, badly wounded, mounted a fine horse and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyue was eating when, startled, he dropped his chopsticks. He was struck in the arm by a short weapon and badly wounded, then mounted a fine horse and fled first.

sentences.zh: 寇兵隨之大潰，相蹂踐死者無數，餘黨悉引去。

translations.literal: The Khitan troops followed in great collapse; countless died trampling one another; the remnant bands all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan troops followed in a great rout. Countless died trampling one another, and the remnant bands all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 契丹自是不敢窺邊，其平居相戒，則曰：當避「黑面大王」，以繼倫面黑故也。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Khitan did not dare again to peer at the frontier; in ordinary times they warned one another, saying they must avoid the "Black-faced Great King" — because Jilun's face was black.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Khitan did not dare again to peer at the frontier. In ordinary times they warned one another to avoid the "Black-faced Great King" — because Jilun's face was black.

sentences.zh: 以功領長州刺史，仍兼巡檢。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the post of prefect of Chang prefecture, while still retaining his inspectorship.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted the post of prefect of Chang prefecture while still retaining his inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，著作佐郎孫崇諫自契丹逃歸，太宗詢以邊事，極言徐河之戰契丹為之奪氣，故每聞繼倫名，則倉皇不知所措。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, Associate Editorial Director Sun Chongjian fled back from the Khitan; Emperor Taizong questioned him about frontier affairs, and he spoke emphatically that at the Battle of Xu River the Khitan had lost their fighting spirit on account of it, so that whenever they heard Jilun's name they became flustered and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era, Associate Editorial Director Sun Chongjian escaped from Khitan territory and returned. Emperor Taizong questioned him about frontier affairs, and he insisted that the Khitan had lost their fighting spirit at the Battle of Xu River—so that whenever they heard Jilun's name they were thrown into panic and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 於是遷繼倫尚食使，領長州團練使，以勵邊將。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jilun was promoted to Commissioner of the Court Commissary and concurrently made regimental commissioner of Chang prefecture, to encourage frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun was then promoted to Commissioner of the Court Commissary and made regimental commissioner of Chang prefecture, as encouragement to frontier generals.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，李繼隆奉詔討夏州，以繼倫為河西兵馬都監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Li Jilong received an edict to campaign against Xia prefecture, and Jilun was made overall supervisor of troops of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Li Jilong received orders to campaign against Xia prefecture, with Jilun appointed overall military supervisor for Hexi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以深州團練使領本州駐泊兵馬部署。

translations.literal: Before long, as regimental commissioner of Shen prefecture he was made deployment commissioner of garrison troops of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became regimental commissioner of Shen prefecture and deployment commissioner of garrison troops there.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，分遣將帥為五道，以討李繼遷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, generals and commanders were dispatched in five columns to campaign against Li Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao, commanders were dispatched in five columns to campaign against Li Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時大將李繼隆由靈環路往，逗撓不進。

translations.literal: At that time the great general Li Jilong went by the Linghuan route but dallied and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Li Jilong took the Linghuan route but dallied and failed to advance.

sentences.zh: 上怒，急召繼倫至京師，授靈、慶兵馬副都部署，欲以夾輔繼隆也。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, urgently summoned Jilun to the capital, and appointed him deputy overall deployment commissioner of troops of Ling and Qing, intending to have him support Jilong from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor urgently summoned Jilun to the capital and appointed him deputy overall deployment commissioner for Ling and Qing, intending him to support Jilong.

sentences.zh: 時繼倫已被病，強起受詔。

translations.literal: At that time Jilun was already ill, but he forced himself to rise and accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun was already ill but forced himself to rise and accept the orders.

sentences.zh: 上素聞其嗜酒，以上尊酒賜而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard of his fondness for wine, and bestowed upon him imperial wine as a gift before sending him off.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his fondness for wine, the emperor bestowed imperial wine on him and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 即日乘驛赴行營，至慶州卒，年五十。

translations.literal: That same day he took post-horses and hastened to the field headquarters; at Qing prefecture he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he rode post-horses to the field headquarters and died at Qing prefecture, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 上聞之嗟悼，賻賵加等，遣中使護其喪而歸葬焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sighed in grief; funeral gifts were increased by one grade, and a palace envoy was sent to escort the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he sighed in grief. Funeral gifts were increased by one grade, and a palace envoy was sent to escort the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 薛超，遼州平城人。

translations.literal: Xue Chao was a native of Pingcheng in Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Chao was from Pingcheng in Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was brave and strong.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，應募為虎捷卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he answered the call for recruits and became a Tiger Swift soldier.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qiande era he enlisted as a Tiger Swift soldier.

sentences.zh: 從崔彥進伐蜀平，錄功補虞候，遷十將。

translations.literal: Following Cui Yanjin in the campaign against Shu until its pacification, his merit was recorded and he was appointed adjutant, then promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cui Yanjin on the campaign against Shu, and after its pacification his service was recognized with appointment as adjutant and promotion to company commander.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，四遷至天武指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted four times to commander of the Tianwu command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was promoted four times to commander of the Tianwu regiment.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，領遊騎千人備禦鎮、定境上，以張軍勢。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Taiyuan, he led a thousand mobile cavalry to guard the borders of Zhen and Ding, to display military strength.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Taiyuan he led a thousand mobile cavalry to guard the borders of Zhen and Ding and display military strength.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還，契丹頻寇鎮、定，侵掠無已。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, the Khitan repeatedly raided Zhen and Ding, plundering without cease.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned, the Khitan repeatedly raided Zhen and Ding, plundering without cease.

sentences.zh: 超從大將劉廷翰率兵至徐河，賊將領騎十餘出挑戰，超躍馬直前，連射數人斃，敵勢遂卻。

translations.literal: Chao followed the great general Liu Tinghan with troops to Xu River; an enemy general led a little over ten horsemen out to challenge; Chao leaped his horse straight forward, shot several men dead in succession, and the enemy's momentum then fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Chao followed General Liu Tinghan to Xu River. An enemy commander led a little over ten horsemen out to challenge him. Chao spurred his horse forward, shot several men dead in succession, and the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 大軍乘之奮擊，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: The main army took advantage and struck fiercely, beheading more than ten thousand.
